text: Everyone came outside and touched grass at once, the most unified moment of the entire run, no cap

The complaints are that it showed up before anything got finished, which is so mid, bestie
Whatever could be carried got passed to whoever could carry it, and the rest was left where it stood with a sticky note saying whose it was, so organized it's giving
Doors got left open, zero locks, pure open-door policy and the vibe check passed for everyone
Food got split up until none was left, the whole pantry went full potluck and nobody was mad about it
Most people wanted to be with their families, and they were, the group chat finally living rent free in real life
People set down whatever they were holding, hands free and unbothered, the era of carrying stuff officially over
The kids got the TLDR version, which is honestly the most bestie thing a parent can do
Dinner went cold on the table while the family who cooked it stood outside staring up, a whole meal left on read
The elders went out to see the end for themselves and came back speechless, the silent era has officially arrived
Nothing new got started, and the vibe was full rest era, no side projects allowed
The final instructions went up where everybody could read them, very clear, very understood the assignment
One of everything got saved, plus a copy of the names, the archive really said keep it real
People said it had been a W of a run for a people, and most of them meant it, no cap
The one thing everybody agreed on was what to leave for whoever came next, and after years of arguing about everything else they settled it in an afternoon, a whole unity arc

In the end they spent the last of it like a holiday that was never coming back, visiting neighbors they had never once talked to and just standing about in doorways, the most delulu bonding arc of all time
A man finally went around to apologize to the brother he had owed one since they were boys, got forgiven on the spot, and was mad about how easy it was, a W too fast to enjoy
The big complaint going around is that the end landed on a weekday, which is so inconsiderate, the group chat is unwell
Factories let the last shift clock out early, a rare W for the workers nobody questioned
Chimneys finally stopped smoking, the air is giving fresh start era
The power station got shut down one boiler at a time, a slow fade with zero drama and full composure
Offices were empty by noon, the 9 to 5 got ghosted before lunch, a real mood
The newspapers ran one last edition, the headlines were so unhinged and so real, a legendary final drop
Last tram of the night did its whole loop with every light on and zero passengers, the loneliest main character solo ride ever
Final paychecks got paid out in full, the bosses ate for once, W for the workers
The works are not reopening Monday, which is so mid for the Monday crew, bestie
Union is cooked and says the end came with zero statutory notice, not even a heads up, which is so rude
The pub crowd is saying it was always going to end like this, and they said that last week too, the prophet arc is not it
Families got photos taken in front of their houses, the whole street went full family photoshoot era, caught in 4K
On the final broadcast a dance band played to an empty studio, the bandleader was giving main character energy for nobody
The men from the rolling mill walked home together in their work clothes for the last time and lingered at the corner before anyone went in, a bro-hug nobody planned and everybody needed

At the town hall the typists stayed late copying out the deeds, the registers and the lists of the dead, so whoever came next would find it all in order and know who had lived there, the archive arc is so wholesome it hurts
The tax office sent its final demands right on schedule, the taxman never misses, so mid and so consistent
Network went down region by region, a slow ghost with zero warning, very mid internet energy
Phones stopped ringing, no more notifs, the silent era has arrived
Most of the final posts were pics of the sky, the whole feed went full aesthetic with zero captions
Final balances froze at midnight, the banks are cooked and nobody saw it coming
Customers are mad that the promised update never shipped, the roadmap was pure delulu and the patch notes are still loading
Staff may keep their company phones, the most generous bestie move the corporation has ever made
Word on the feeds is the corporations knew and sold tickets anyway, the whole thing is sus and we're not even surprised
The delivery drones got called home and parked in neat rows on the pads, blinking like confused little cuties
Fusion plants got brought down one after another and the city dimmed in stages over three nights, a slow fade with main character lighting

In the arcades the kids who had grinded one game every night for years played it one last time together, then left the cabinets on, demo screens looping for an empty room, the nostalgia arc hits different
Screens across the city went dark one block at a time, the skyline was ghosted block by block, I'm deceased
Every server farm stayed on for as long as the power held, humming to itself in the dark, the most dedicated little hum ever, bet
People stayed logged in to the end, doomscrolling through years of their own posts and pics, a full chronically online farewell tour
All personal files will be kept in the permanent archive, your camera roll is immortal now, so no delete button for the bad selfies

The last message went out to every address the city had ever held, including the dead ones from years back, and said thank you and goodbye in every language anyone there had ever spoken, the most wholesome send-all ever, I'm deceased
Orbital yards got shut down, the space dock is officially cooked
Launches got cancelled, the sky said nah, and the countdown got a big fat L
The last shuttle up carried seed stock, photos and not much else, the ultimate pack-light moment, understood the assignment
Stations got mothballed, crews rotated home, orbits logged, the whole space arc wrapped up neat and bussin
Every craft is ordered home to dock and power down, even the ships have to touch grass
The moon base is salty it was told last, the lunar crew felt so left on read
On the station they say the view never looked better, the stars are giving main character lighting on the way out
The mining crews came in from the belt, the asteroid grind finally ended, no cap, they earned the rest
Ring station got turned so its windows faced home, and the crew took turns at them through the last watch, a whole cozy era moment in orbit

Up in orbit the satellites got left running solo, still beaming down weather pics of cities where the streets had emptied and the lights went off one district at a time, the most dedicated background character ever
Mission control signed off, the final sign-off was so chill, peace out
The far side crew heard last of all over a delayed signal and wrote down every word by hand, the lag is real and the notes are immaculate
Fuel got poured back into the tanks, the rockets are saving it for a comeback arc, big plan energy
The orbital hotel refunded its bookings, less a handling fee, the most mid billing move in the whole sky
Kids at the observation windows waved at the ships coming in until the last one docked, the most bestie send-off the sky has ever seen
The final word went to {subject}, and it was not even close, the ending is their whole personality
Out past the last charted star something stirred, the way a sleeper stirs when a door shuts in another room, lowkey the scariest vibe check of all
Through the whole shutdown {subject} stayed, watching, the ultimate lurker era
The dark came closer and the vibes went full horror movie, sus and cooked

Whatever waits at the end of all roads had been told the colony was coming, and the last thing the long-range instruments logged before shutdown was a patch of sky where the background noise went silent, that is so sus
The crew is mad that {subject} never said what comes after, a total cliffhanger with zero follow-up, very mid
All logs stay open for {subject} to read, they are literally the main character of the logbook now
People on the command deck say {subject} knew the hour all along, and honestly the timing was giving prophet energy
The stars went on, completely unbothered, living rent free in the sky
Air normal, power falling, every soul accounted for, the roll call was so clean
When the colony's last lights went out, {subject} stayed up in the dark after everyone had gone to bed, the night owl grind is real
The instruments kept recording after everyone stopped reading them, a dedicated stan with no audience left
Colony ended its watch, a whole shift of vigilance finally clocked out
Right up to the end {subject} gave no comfort and no blame, just pure unbothered energy

Far past the colony's instruments, where only one probe still reported, the thing it had been warned about for four ages turned away without rushing, and the probe lost track of it within the hour, the plot twist nobody saw coming and nobody enjoyed
Engineering filed its last maintenance request, marked urgent, the most dedicated ticket energy in the galaxy
The colonists took turns sitting with {subject} through the last watch, and none of them could say afterwards what got said, the vibe was so deep it was basically a secret
Kids slept right through it, the most unbothered gen alpha nap ever, no cap
The hydroponics bays got left lit, the plants are giving main character glow and they know it
At the end the only voice left on comms was {subject}, the lone chat in the room, you love to see it
The old hands say the dark had been patient long enough, and that it was only ever waiting for the colony to stop, the lurker finally got its moment
Beacon's loop ended with your name, it had you in its top 8 for real
After the last lights went out the beacon kept looping, and the loop is giving main character forever
For eighty years the beacon had been warning everyone, and at the end it just added the colony to its list, the prophet grind finally paid off

The dead colony's beacon and the living colony's last transmission overlapped for a few seconds, two recordings of the end playing over each other on one frequency, and then the living one cut out, the group call nobody wanted to be on
Honestly the comms officer swears the beacon said goodbye, the most bestie thing a signal has ever done
Beacon still transmitting, colony left on read
The relay folded the colony into its geometry and went quiet, so big-brain it hurts
Linguists stayed at their posts to translate the last of it, the nerd era is finally paying off
Relay's hum held one note, a steady vibe with zero fluctuation

The relay had said this to others before, and the linguists found the colony's own name already written into its oldest geometry, among peoples who ended long before anyone here learned to talk, a whole ancient era that's sus and cooked
Linguists are mad that the relay's last message has no verb, the grammar is giving unfinished fanfic
Keep the relay powered after we're gone, bestie this is the legacy move
Your future self sent nothing this time, the ultimate left-on-read move
From nine years out came one last message, and it was just your own breathing, the most awkward voicemail ever left
Your future self said this is the part you always forget, so please try to remember it this time, we are literally begging you
Timestamps on your future self's messages had been running backwards for weeks, closer to today each time, and at the end they stopped right there, the timeline is cooked and we're not even surprised
Your future self said it was worth it, and you chose to believe that, delulu is the solution

In the last hour a message came from nine years out in your own handwriting, letters a little wrong like the hand had been out of practice, and it said only that it was glad you stayed up, the most emotional plot twist of the run
Your unmade self took your hand, the most unhinged but wholesome bonding moment across all of time
This is how mine ended too, it said, and it did not let go, the parallel self is giving a whole cautionary tale
The branch you stood on and the branch that ended finally met, the timeline reunion nobody asked for and everybody needed

Your unmade self came all this way to see whether this branch ends the way its own did, stayed to watch it do exactly that, and seemed almost relieved to have company, the main character had a whole support group
Half the station is mad that the other you never explains itself, the whole vibe is mysterious and extremely sus
